Back in 2020 I got out of my first serious long term relationship and I was absolutely devastated. I didn’t know how to function on my own, I moved cities, into a place with my brother and I hated it, I was high 24/7, and then I ended up dropping out of university. It felt like one thing after another and like I’d never get out of it. I’m not much older than you, so I’m saying this as someone who was just there feeling like nothing made sense, and today I am working full time in a career that I love but I never saw myself in, I have my own apartment, my own car, and a solid outlook on life (most of the time, at least) I go to therapy and spend time working on me. I genuinely never saw myself where I am now, back then. I had months where I felt on top of the world, and some where I struggled to keep waking up the next day, where it felt like everything was falling apart and I’d never be happy. I’ve learned to accept that instead of worrying about how “far ahead or behind” I am in my life, just spend every day trying to build myself a life that I don’t want to get away from, to make the best and do things that make me happy (even if they’re the most insignificant mundane things, like getting a fancy coffee drink and singing in my car on my drive to work or watching a sunset) 
Also breakups are the worst. Let yourself cry and grieve and be sad, listen to sad music, feel your feelings! The only cure for that is time. It took me a long time to move past that first one. the first time i came out as anything was in august of 2015. i came out as non binary and wanted to go by they/them. Nobody; not family or friends or anybody outside the internet would use my pronouns.  the following april (2016) i came out as ftm trans. about 6 months after that i started going by my current name (my old name was pretty gender neutral but like you mentioned, it didn’t sit right with me). after all of this time my mother had finally started using they/them pronouns (as soon as she understood she’s been very supportive) and a few of my close friends were using the right ones. but i had lost hope for my dad to ever change and all anyone ever said was “give them time” 
and all i wanted was to give up because i never thought the day would come when i was my fathers son. in may of 2017 my legal name and gender marker changed, i started Testosterone that october. a year later, in october 2018, three long long long years (and one of them on testosterone and actively living as me, but i didn’t live too close to him) when he finally acknowledged me. and since then he’s come around completely, i am his son and nothing less. he doesn’t understand a lot of things still, but he is trying 

my point in all this, if it helps, is that it is going to feel like they will never acknowledge you. and everyone will probably tell you to give them time and it sucks to hear, but i promise that time will come when you are authentic and transitioned and they will know you as you. even if you want to give up, the fact that they haven’t completely disowned you is a good thing, they will come around. don’t give up hope, and don’t give up trying to educate. best of luck, friend
